title: Fix incorrect calculation of next buffer size in AdaptiveRecvByteBufAllocator

timeline.author: bruce

timeline.body: Can one of the admins verify this patch?
Can we also assert the guess incrementing after the read bytes increases?

reply.body: yes, But I think my unit test is correct.
I'm not saying it's incorrect, but it only asserts in one direction.
Maybe method ``rampUpBeforeReadCompleteWhenLargeDataPending`` contains the assertions you need.
Point was to test going down and up to ensure the predicted buffer size is adaptive.
After playing with this a bit I feel the unit test is flawed as it does not take into consideration the index increment and decrement step.

timeline.body: The fix looks correct to me and probably what was originally intended, but would be good to get confirmation from original author (@trustin I think!)

> The fix looks correct to me and probably what was originally intended, but would be good to get confirmation from original author (@trustin I think!)

Wouldn't it make more sense to calculate the predicted buffer size using steps and the table instead of asserting random values?
@johnou I was referring to the fix itself, I don't disagree with your comments about the unit test... sorry I should have also added that caveat to my approval!
TBH I don't remember the reasoning behind this bug (or not) anymore :sweat_smile: The fix seems OK to me though. Would be nice to have a better test case, as commented by @johnou.
@trustin @johnou  The program I modified meets all the original unit tests. If the unit tests are not perfect, then the original unit tests are not perfect.
Let me merge the fix and Improve the unit test as a followup to make progress
Thanks @brucelwl for your patience. +1 for moving forward.
